blogs.title: Bridging vessels or blood? Sorting degenerating fibroids from decidualized endometriomas in pregnancy
blogs.description: A practical imaging playbook for pregnant patients with large adnexal-appearing cysts: how to use ultrasound with color Doppler (bridging vessels, claw sign, peripheral flow), and non-contrast MRI (T1/T2 shading, cystic degeneration patterns, mural nodules) to distinguish leiomyomas with cystic change from decidualized endometriomas. We’ll cover why gravid anatomy obscures stalks/feeding vessels, common pitfalls that mimic malignancy, and how serial imaging tightens the diagnosis when tissue isn’t an immediate option.

blogs.title: When to cut: Indications, timing, and approach for myomectomy during pregnancy
blogs.description: A decision framework for intervening on large, symptomatic uterine masses in the second trimester: balancing pain, torsion/rupture/infection risk, and respiratory compromise against obstetric risk. We’ll compare laparoscopy vs laparotomy selection criteria, outline operative tactics (short cases, minimal uterine manipulation, hemostasis without uterine vasoconstrictors), anesthesia pearls (left uterine displacement, aspiration risk), VTE prophylaxis, and standardized fetal heart assessment before/after (and, when feasible, during) surgery.

blogs.title: CA-125 and friends in pregnancy: how not to be fooled by tumor markers
blogs.description: Why single-timepoint CA-125 values mislead in pregnancy and how to interpret trends in context. We’ll review trimester-specific physiology, benign causes of elevation (leiomyomas, endometriosis, decidualization, infection), and limitations of common risk models and markers (e.g., O-RADS, ROMA/HE4) in pregnancy. Practical guidance on integrating markers with imaging and clinical trajectory to calibrate oncologic suspicion and avoid unnecessary intervention.

blogs.title: Breathless from below: diagnosing mass-effect dyspnoea in pregnancy
blogs.description: An approach to dyspnoea in pregnancy when massive pelvic or subphrenic lesions compress the diaphragm. We’ll differentiate mechanical restriction from cardiopulmonary causes at the bedside, choose pregnancy-safe imaging, and use supportive measures (positioning, analgesia) while planning definitive management. Case-based thresholds for decompression when symptoms and mass size escalate despite conservative care.

blogs.title: Plan the birth, not just the operation: delivery strategy with residual large fibroids
blogs.description: How mass size, number, and location reshape delivery planning: predicting labor obstruction (lower uterine segment/cervico-isthmic and posterior masses), deciding between trial of labor and scheduled cesarean, and when to defer myomectomy vs perform cesarean myomectomy. We’ll discuss hemorrhage risk counseling, incision choices, and postpartum regression to time interval myomectomy only if symptoms persist.

blogs.title: Perioperative obstetric co-management: fetal monitoring, tocolysis, and antibiotic stewardship
blogs.description: A protocolized checklist for non-obstetric surgery in pregnancy: fetal heart rate documentation pre/post (and intraop when feasible), anesthesia and positioning considerations, analgesia choices avoiding NSAIDs after 20 weeks, and selective—not routine—tocolysis. We’ll examine the lack of evidence for prophylactic progesterone/17-OHPC after surgery, and outline culture-guided, pregnancy-safe antibiotic strategies for UTIs and surgical prophylaxis.
